newsitem.title: USA: IMF chief sees continued world economic upswing.
newsitem.headline: IMF chief sees continued world economic upswing.

text.p: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus Thursday called the chances of continued world economic expansion "good."
"The world economy is now in a favorable situation," he told the closing session of the IMF/World Bank annual meeting. "The prospects for continued global expansion are good."

In its recently published World Economic Outlook, the IMF had predicted a steady increase in world growth to 4.1 percent in 1997 after 3.8 percent in 1996 and 3.5 percent in 1995 and said it expected inflation to stay under control.

Camdessus said in his speech that stronger economic policies and action taken to reduce deficits, create jobs and eliminate structural problems had helped to promote growth, but added that more must be done to address such issues.

Yet the very pace of economic globalisation was prompting nations to take such steps to remain competitive. "The rapid pace of global integration and its impact on world trade and finance has inspired many countries to accelerate reform."
Camdessus welcomed a declaration from the IMF's Interim Committee laying down its aims and conditions for continued growth in the light of increased globalisation.
He said increased surveillance -- close observation of economic developments in the Fund's 181 member countries, was now "more relevant than ever".
He welcomed calls from the annual meeting to strengthen the Fund's resources and pledged that reform of the Bretton Woods institutions would continue.
"Let us keep our sights on our common goals: greater stability in the world, and stronger, more sustained, more broadly shared, and higher quality growth," he added.
